items.title: Supreme Court cautions lawyers against responding "belligerently" to questions asked by judges
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Thursday said that lawyers should not assume that every question put by a judge is an adversarial stance against their client, and should refrain from responding belligerently to such queries by the court [ P Kathirvel vs. State ]. A Bench of Justices JB Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran recorded its disapproval of the conduct of a Senior Advocate appearing in a case. The Bench noted that he took umbrage at the Court's queries and repeatedly accused the judges of not hearing him. "We mention this only to caution the minority in the bar, who takes every syllable uttered by a judge to be a stance taken against the client he represents in court and respond acrimoniously to the bench." it noted . The Bench stressed that counsel must assist the court in a non-acrimonious manner rather than placing judges in an adversarial position. "It would be always in the fitness of things to carry on the assistance in a non- acrimonious mood, which the majority of the Bar realise, and do not place the courts in an adversarial role. items.title: Delhi HC slams MHA for not disclosing "secret" inputs that led to cancellation of NGO's FCRA license
items.summary: The Delhi High Court on Thursday criticised the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) for not disclosing, even to the court, the “security inputs” which formed the basis for cancellation of the Foreign Contribution Regulation Act (FCRA) registration of NGO Socio-Legal Information Centre (SLIC). SLIC is a non-governmental organisation (NGO) that describes itself as a legal aid and education organisation. In his order, Justice Anup Jairam Bhambhani noted that the NGO faced drastic action because of these security inputs, adding that they cannot be kept secret to the point that no material is shown even to the Court. “While the respondent [government] contends that the violations on the appellant’s [NGO’s] part were brought to its notice through ‘security inputs’, which cannot be divulged since they are ‘secret’; this court is of the view that such inputs cannot be kept secret to the point that no material is brought even to the notice of this court, though the appellant has faced the drastic action of having its FCRA registration cancelled, arising from such inputs,” the Court said. items.title: PMLA Adjudicating Authority cannot confirm ED's property attachment without judicial member: Supreme Court
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Thursday ruled that the adjudicating authority confirming the provisional attachment of properties by the Enforcement Directorate (ED) under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA) must include a judicial member. A Bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana also ruled that the attachment cannot be confirmed by a single-member adjudicating authority unless that member is a judicial member. The Bench observed that the adjudication carries substantial consequences for the civil and consequential constitutional rights of the person whose property has been attached by the ED. "If the Adjudicating Authority finds that the property is involved in money laundering, the provisions of Sections 8(3) and 8(4) are attracted and possession of the property is taken over by the Government of India. Such dispossession may well endure until the conclusion of the trial for the offence of money laundering, depriving the person of the use of the property for a considerable period before the offence is proved," the Court said. Thus, the Court said that the presence of a judicial member on the bench would ensure legal objectivity

items.title: UK court grants bail to Indian lawyer Vijay Aggarwal on £500,000 bond in sexual assault case
items.summary: A court in the United Kingdom on Wednesday granted bail to prominent Indian criminal lawyer Vijay Aggarwal in a case involving allegations of rape and sexual assault. Judge David Tomlinson of the Southwark Crown Court also granted bail to Aggarwal's assistant Manpreet Kaur, who is a co-accused in the case. Aggarwal was directed to furnish a bond of £500,000 while Kaur was directed to furnish a bond of £200,000. Both have been barred from travelling outside the United Kingdom. Aggarwal and Kaur were present in court during the hearing. Aggarwal's wife, daughter and son-in-law were also present. Aggarwal and Kaur were arrested by the Metropolitan Police on August 11 from a property in London's Mayfair area . The arrests followed complaints of sexual assault in connection with incidents alleged to have occurred on May 26 and August 9 this year. Aggarwal currently faces one charge of rape and three charges of sexual assault. Southwark Crown Court had earlier rejected Aggarwal's bail application on September 23 on the ground that he posed a flight risk. A Bench of Justices Aravind Kumar and Vipul Pancholi suspended the current board of trustees of the Subramaniya Swami Temple for defying the Court's directions. It then proceeded to appoint retired Justices S Vaidyanathan and V Parthiban as receivers of the trust of the temple and directed that the Karthigai Deepam be lit at the Deepathoon tomorrow, November 28. The Court directed the court-appointed receivers, entrusted with the administration of the temple after the supersession of its board of trustees, to ensure the lighting of the lamp. The security of the temple perimeter was directed to be handed over to the Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF). items.title: Small mercies and large silences: The Supreme Court and the Constitution at 77
items.summary: Every November 26, the Supreme Court’s lawns are scrubbed, the ceremonial speeches are dusted off and the Republic congratulates itself on the durability of its founding charter. Constitution Day invites easy theatrics. Critics declare the document dead on arrival; loyalists hail the bench as an infallible shield against executive excess. The Supreme Court’s record across 2026 resists both caricatures. Over the past 11 months, the Court has displayed a striking split personality. When confronting the daily, retail indignities inflicted on ordinary citizens by municipal apathy, police high-handedness or bureaucratic drift, the Court has been remarkably imaginative. Yet, when asked to scrutinise the institutional architecture of democracy itself, the same Court has repeatedly blinked, deferred or stalled in the vestibule. The guardian of the sidewalk Take the Court’s record on individual dignity and personal liberty this year and there is genuine constitutional craftsmanship to admire. items.summary: After four days of public outcry and strong opposition from political parties, the Tamil Nadu police arrested Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) MLA C Arul Vignesh on November 27 for allegedly sexually harassing a woman IAS officer. A police team led by Investigating officer Shristi Singh arrested the MLA from his residence. Before the arrest, the MLA’s residence was cordoned off and a large number of police were deployed to take him into custody. A First Information Report (FIR) was registered against him at the All Women Police Station (AWPS) in Kallakurichi on November 24. The MLA has been booked under sections 75 (sexual harassment), 78(2) (stalking) and 132 (assault or use of criminal force to deter a public servant from discharging their duty) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), along with Section 4 of Prevention of Sexual Harassment (PoSH) Act. The case was registered after the woman IAS officer submitted a written complaint to Tamil Nadu Chief Secretary M Sai Kumar on November 23 under the PoSH Act. items.title: SC orders lamp to be lit at Thiruparankundram Deepathoon on Nov 28, suspends temple trustees
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Friday suspended the board of trustees of the Thiruparankundram temple in Madurai district and ordered that the Karthigai Deepam be lit at the disputed pillar or Deepathoon on Saturday, November 28, after its earlier order was not carried out. A Bench of Justices Aravind Kumar and Vipul M Pancholi appointed former High Court judges Justice S Vaidyanathan and Justice V Parthipan as receivers to administer the temple, according to the Live Law. They have to ensure that the lamp is lit, using the flame at Uchipillaiyar. The Supreme Court has also handed over the security of the entire hill to the Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF), citing the failure of the Tamil Nadu Police to implement its orders. The court has directed CRPF to ensure the peaceful functioning of the temple and the Dargah. A Siva temple and the Uchi Pillaiyar temple are located on the lower part of the Tirupurakundram hill, while the dargah stands at its summit. For decades, the customary Karthigai Deepam has been lit near the Uchi Pillaiyar Temple by the temple management.
